1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. What the exam is. The three domains and their weights. Where each domain lives in this course. How to read the exam wording. A repeatable way to answer a question. A study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All three domains. Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: What the exam is
1.text: What the exam is. The A Z nine hundred exam tests foundational knowledge of cloud concepts and of Microsoft Azure. It is a common first step toward an Azure career. You do not need to build anything: you need to describe and recognize services, models and tools and pick the right one for a short scenario.

1.title: What the exam is, continued
1.text: What the exam is. Time. forty-five minutes for the assessment. Passing score. seven hundred or more, on a scale of one to one thousand. Retake. twenty-four hours after the first attempt; later waits vary. Languages. English first; other languages follow about eight weeks later. Number of questions, price, question types. not on the pages this course was built from: confirm on the exam page. The price depends on the country or region. Note. A scaled score of seven hundred does not mean seventy percent of the questions. Do not try to compute a percentage; aim to understand everything in the study guide.

1.title: What the exam is, continued
1.text: What the exam is. The figure shows this: The A Z nine hundred exam at a glance: three domains and their weights.

1.title: The three domains and their weights
1.text: The three domains and their weights. Describe cloud concepts. Weight: twenty-five to thirty percent. What it asks: What cloud computing is, why it is used, and the service types (I A A S, pass, sass). Describe Azure architecture and services. Weight: thirty-five to forty percent. What it asks: Regions, zones, resource organization, compute, networking, storage, identity and security. Describe Azure management and governance. Weight: thirty to thirty-five percent. What it asks: Cost, governance and compliance, tools for managing resources, monitoring. The middle domain is the biggest, but the other two together are more than half of the exam. Every domain matters.

1.title: Where each domain lives in this course
1.text: Where each domain lives in this course. one, two, three. Domain: Cloud concepts. Skills groups: cloud computing; benefits; service types. four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Domain: Architecture and services. Skills groups: core components; compute and networking; storage; identity, access and security. eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen. Domain: Management and governance. Skills groups: cost; governance and compliance; managing and deploying resources; monitoring. fifteen. Domain: All. Skills groups: exam technique and a final review.

1.title: How to read the exam wording
1.text: How to read the exam wording. The exam uses action words. Each one tells you the depth you need. Define. Give the meaning in one sentence. Describe. Explain what it is, what it is for and one key fact. Compare. Tell two or more options apart and say when to pick each. Identify. Pick the right option from a list (often use cases). Explore. Know what the tool shows (for example the pricing calculator). Exam tip: "Identify appropriate use cases" means the question gives a business need and you choose the cloud model, service type or service that fits. Learn each service with its one-line purpose.

1.title: A repeatable way to answer a question
1.text: A repeatable way to answer a question. Read the last sentence first. It tells you what is asked (which service, which model, which benefit). Underline the key need: "no servers to manage", "keep data in the country", "pay only for what you use", "control access to resources". Remove options that are clearly another category: for example a storage service in a networking question. Pick the most specific match, not the most powerful service. Mark and move on if you are stuck. forty-five minutes is short; do not stay on one question.

1.title: A study plan
1.text: A study plan. one. What to do: Learn the vocabulary of the cloud first: models, benefits, service types. Modules: one to three. two. What to do: Learn the Azure building blocks: regions, resources, compute, network, storage. Modules: four to eight. three. What to do: Learn how identity and security fit together. Modules: nine to ten. four. What to do: Learn cost, governance, tools and monitoring. Modules: eleven to fourteen. five. What to do: Review with the Quick Reference Cards and the practice questions. Modules: fifteen. Spaced review: after each module, answer its recall questions from memory, then check. Repeat each Quick Reference Card the next day and again after a week.

1.title: What is not on the exam
1.text: What is not on the exam. The exam is foundational. It does not ask you to write code, build a network, or configure a service step by step. Detailed portal clicks and command syntax are out of scope; this course mentions a command only to show what a tool does.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors is planning for the A Z nine hundred exam and wants to know which domain carries the largest weight. Which domain is it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Describe Azure architecture and services. Describe Azure architecture and services is thirty-five to forty percent, the largest range. Cloud concepts is twenty-five to thirty percent and management and governance is thirty to thirty-five percent.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A candidate scores seven hundred on the exam. What does that mean? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The candidate reached the passing score on a scale of one to one thousand. seven hundred or more on a scale of one to one thousand is a pass. The scaled score is not a percentage of correct answers.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A question asks you to "identify appropriate use cases" for a cloud service type. What is expected? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Match a business need to the service type or service that fits it. Identify means to choose the right option for a described need. Commands, prices and diagrams are not what the verb asks for.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. During the exam you reach a question you cannot answer after a minute of thought. What is the best action? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Mark it, make your best choice, move on and return if time remains. The exam is forty-five minutes, so time is limited. Give a best answer, mark it and return later.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How long is the A Z nine hundred assessment? Answer: forty-five minutes. Question two. What score passes, and on what scale? Answer: seven hundred or more on a scale of one to one thousand. Question three. Name the three domains and their weights. Answer: Cloud concepts twenty-five to thirty percent, Azure architecture and services thirty-five to forty percent, Azure management and governance thirty to thirty-five percent.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. After how long can you retake a failed exam for the first time? Answer: twenty-four hours after the first attempt. Question five. Which part of the question do you read first? Answer: The last sentence, because it says what is asked. Question six. Does the exam ask for step-by-step configuration? Answer: No. It is foundational: you describe, compare and identify.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Format: forty-five minutes; pass at seven hundred of one thousand; retake after twenty-four hours. Domains: cloud concepts twenty-five to thirty percent; architecture and services thirty-five to forty percent; management and governance thirty to thirty-five percent. Verbs: define, describe, compare, identify, explore. Method: read the last sentence, find the key need, remove other categories, pick the most specific match, mark and move on. Scope: foundational: no code and no step-by-step builds. In the next module, we continue the course.
